Whole-package review protocol

Source: PACKAGE_REVIEW.md

Use this protocol only for an explicitly commissioned deep review of usRds. Its presence does not start an audit. REVIEWING.md defines shared review standards and remains the guide for routine PR reviews. Read AGENTS.md and applicable subdirectory guidance. This protocol does not grant implementation, posting, approval, merge or automation permissions.

Adapted from the whole-package protocols in sRtr at 2d0b878 and CDCAtlas at 3c02b95, with usRds-specific clinical coverage, source requirements and data boundaries.

Purpose and scope

Assess current implementation, scientific definitions, complete user workflows, documentation, tests and CI, every open issue, and justified future needs. Ask whether users can obtain invalid analyses even when code works as written. Distinguish verified defects, evidence gaps, methodological choices, intentional unfinished work, documentation problems and optional enhancements.

Review does not authorize fixes or selection of scientific defaults. It does include independent synthetic checks and concrete proposed documentation, regression-test and CI patches. Keep these separate from the frozen baseline. Install permanent changes only through the maintainer’s authorized workflow.

1. Freeze the target and establish safe execution

Record repository, verified default branch, full commit SHA, date, package version, policy revision, comparison scope, website URL and observed deployment revision if available. For PRs use target-branch policy at its recorded SHA and the merge base; proposed policy does not govern its own review. Whole-package scope covers the complete frozen package, not only its latest diff. GitHub scope excludes unpushed work. For a requested local review, inventory staged, unstaged and relevant untracked changes read-only; execute only in an isolated workspace.

Never access, copy, upload or expose restricted patient-level data. Never run real-data tests, even if enabled by environment variables. The connected working copy, synced sources and active RStudio session remain read-only. Inspect data-raw/ source without running regeneration; never edit or regenerate data/ or R/sysdata.rda. For uncertain fixture provenance, report only its path and request verification without opening values.

Before loading package code, inspect startup files, R/zzz.R and other load hooks, test helpers, setup files, guards and call sites for data access or writes. Inspect tests/testthat/helper-live.R for the actual live-test variables at the reviewed revision; do not assume one guard protects all paths. Unset USRDS_WD, disable/unset all discovered live-data switches and exclude checks whose real data access cannot be ruled out. Do not copy private startup settings.

Use a fresh Rscript –vanilla process. Set R_ENVIRON_USER and R_PROFILE_USER to empty files in the isolated workspace for child processes as well. Retain those files for the entire run. Verify parent and child startup isolation using harmless synthetic startup files before relying on package checks, and record the result. Recheck effective guards where helpers can restore settings. Keep caches and incidental outputs in temporary locations. No check may use the maintainer’s active session or real-data directories.

Use only small, obviously synthetic fixtures with documented columns and provenance. Synthetic checks establish code behavior, not validity on actual USRDS releases. Report exact blockers and safe remaining maintainer commands without requesting patient-level output.

2. Required review perspectives

Use independent reviewer contexts where supported, scheduling roles in waves when necessary. These are AI specialist perspectives, not claims of clinical credentials or replacements for authoritative sources and human expertise. Record unavailable roles or lack of independence as coverage limitations.

At minimum, clinical review must include separate dialysis and transplant expert perspectives. Neither can be replaced by a generic clinical reviewer.

Perspective Required coverage
Dialysis clinician-researcher Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis; incident/prevalent cohorts; modality and facility transitions; treatment episodes; dialysis access and complications; hospitalization, mortality and ascertainment limits
Transplant clinician-researcher Kidney transplantation, functioning graft versus graft failure, return to dialysis, retransplantation, sequential/multiorgan transplantation, post-transplant follow-up and applicability of shared definitions
USRDS and Medicare claims methodology specialist Release-specific guides and appendices, file/field meanings, payer and eligibility histories, claims availability, coding eras, linkage and units of observation
Biostatistician and epidemiologist Time origins, time-varying covariates, lookback, censoring, competing events, repeated episodes, missingness, selection and ascertainment bias
Health economist or claims-cost methods reviewer Payment versus charges, claim versus revenue-line amounts, overlap, proration, negative adjustments, inflation and monetary perspective
R package and data engineer Exported/internal functions, SAS/CSV/Parquet behavior, identifiers, joins, labels, attributes, dependencies, errors, side effects, performance evidence and Windows behavior
Independent testing and reproducibility reviewer Test expectations, fixtures, mocks, integration coverage, skips, startup isolation, CI configuration and observed runs; concrete regression-test and CI proposals
Scientific librarian and provenance reviewer Source coverage, editions, locators, actual reading status, contradictions, external code provenance and reference maintenance
Researcher using the package Website, README, help and vignettes; discoverability, explanations, practical misuse risks and complete workflows

Add infectious diseases, oncology, pharmacy, pediatric, spatial or other specialists when the inventory warrants them. Do not invent capabilities to fill roles. Dialysis and transplant reviewers must both assess shared logic for dialysis-to-transplant transitions, graft failure/return to dialysis, retransplantation, mortality and follow-up. Claims, statistical and engineering reviewers independently challenge the corresponding representations and timing.

The coordinator assigns every in-scope file/function, verifies findings, reconciles disagreements and tracks coverage. No single specialist must read everything. Agreement among reviewers is not scientific evidence.

3. Reference use and independent first passes

Use reference/README.md as the single guide to source selection, placement and citation. Inventory the actual files at the frozen revision, including:

  • Official sources.
  • Manuscript catalog and linked annotations.
  • External code.
  • Methodological background.

The coordinator and librarian map the full catalog to review topics and identify coverage gaps. A catalog of 100 manuscripts is not proof that all were fully read or that every package definition is supported. Record relevant sources selected, sources screened out with a reason, unread material and access gaps. Do not require every reviewer to reread every paper; do require substantive verification of the sources supporting their consequential conclusions.

Prepare topic-specific packets with primary-source links, editions, study periods, population, units, exact sections/tables and pinned external-code locations. Include both dialysis and transplant literature. Distinguish defining sources, published conventions and external implementations. Verify the underlying source rather than treating annotations as authority. Recheck exact field/code names against a named release. Publication year is not data vintage; 2025 documentation does not automatically establish older-release definitions. Check unclear converted tables against originals and disclose unavailable guides, appendices or supplements.

For initial independent passes, withhold prior package diagnoses, issue conclusions and other reviewers’ findings. Existing source, tests and neutral reference facts remain available. Do not pass annotated judgments wholesale and claim blindness; disclose unavoidable exposure. Private conversations and handoffs are coordinator context only and must not be published.

External code is source-inspection evidence, not scientific authority or permission to open its data. Follow reference/README.md’s provenance boundaries. Record new sources and reconcile useful background into existing reference entries. Keep package defects and implementation decisions in their owning issues, tests or documentation.

For each consequential scientific conclusion record source, edition/era, locator, what was actually read, what it supports, uncertainties, and the definition or check it informs. A bibliography alone does not satisfy this.

4. Inventory, trace and assess definitions

Inventory all tracked files, exported/internal functions, tests/helpers, documentation, workflows, reference records, and open issues/PRs. Paginate collections and reconcile counts. Inspect relevant closed issues and merged PRs for prior resolutions. Keep unmerged fixes distinct from current behavior.

Maintain a resumable coverage record outside the repository:

Item Revision Assigned perspectives Read Source verification Executed checks Disposition/gap

Read every in-scope human-written source and documentation file, not a sample. Check generated documentation against source; inventory binaries without opening uncertain data. State exclusions and reasons. “Not assessed” remains a coverage gap. On resumption, reuse records and recheck intervening changes; a fresh audit must not merely rerun an old bundle.

Trace loading -> labeling/missingness -> linkage -> eligibility/cohort creation -> derived measures -> analysis-ready output. Compare documented contracts, implementation, callers, returned attributes and complete workflows.

For each scientific definition or derived measure, record population and unit, source files/fields, codes, dates/time units, release, missingness, eligibility, timing, censoring, assumptions, implementation and test coverage. Require: clinical/methodological validity, support from the applicable source, and correct implementation. Preserve disagreements and identify evidence or a maintainer decision needed to settle them.

Apply REVIEWING.md’s usRds-specific checks, emphasizing:

  • Person, treatment episode, transplant, encounter, claim and revenue-line units; identifier precision, duplicate keys and join multiplication.
  • Cross-format and cross-release layouts, column selection, labels versus codes, distinct missing categories, partial years and stale session state.
  • Eligibility and payer history versus administrative follow-up and observable claims; ICD era, exact/prefix matching, positions and distinct encounters.
  • Dialysis modality transitions, graft failure, return to dialysis, retransplantation and row-varying supplied baselines versus patient-specific default baselines. Preserve cohort attributes and finalization state.
  • Costs by named measure: payment/charge distinctions, overlap, proration conservation, partial windows, negative adjustments and inflation coverage.

Do not transfer an individual analysis’s inclusion, matching or endpoint rules into package defaults without a decision. Compare meaningful alternatives on the same synthetic inputs when useful; label decision-dependent expectations.

5. Website and documentation

Give the researcher perspective the published site and help first, before code. Read every article/vignette, README and exported-function help page. Then compare with the frozen implementation. Assess:

  • Whether a researcher can follow installation and complete a workflow without unstated prerequisites; use synthetic substitutes where execution is safe.
  • Whether USRDS the data source and usRds the package are clearly distinguished.
  • Whether units, coverage assumptions, missingness, costs and follow-up choices are explained, including when defaults are unsuitable.
  • Whether examples use the current API and output, and all exported functions appear in the reference index.
  • Whether the deployed site matches the reviewed revision; distinguish source inspection, an isolated build and observed deployment.
  • Links, citations, headings, meaningful alt text, readable tables and color independence. Check Markdown/LLM copies if present.
  • Whether root review files or other unintended content are published. .Rbuildignore excludes files from package builds, not necessarily pkgdown.

Record passage, problem, likely consequence and proposed rewrite. Keep explanatory shortcomings distinct from calculation defects; code/help conflicts must identify which contract needs a decision. Do not execute real-data vignettes to complete this workstream.

6. Independent tests and CI

Audit every test/helper and workflow. Map coverage to definitions, functions and end-to-end workflows. Derive expected results from sources and hand-worked synthetic examples independently of implementation. Challenge mocks that bypass the claimed behavior, unjustified skips and assertions that encode the same bug.

Create useful synthetic reproducers for serious suspected defects and uncovered high-risk behavior. Preserve their inputs, source basis, exact commands, dependencies and observed results separately from the frozen package. Distinguish passing, failing, decision-dependent and blocked/not-run checks. Do not weaken assertions or silently fix implementation to make an audit pass.

Inspect CI triggers/path filters, actual tested revisions, R/OS matrices, dependency handling, permissions, secrets use, caches, skips, timeouts and failure propagation. Inspect required-check settings if available and disclose access gaps. Configuration is not evidence of execution; a pkgdown build is not a full package check. Assess installation, exports, synthetic format equivalence, Windows paths and meaningful integration coverage.

Deliver concrete permanent-test or inert workflow patches for material gaps, with destination, rationale, expected signal, prerequisites and validation status; if none are warranted, explain why. Strengthen existing tests/workflows before creating new infrastructure. Keep proposed workflow changes inert until authorized. Do not create a second permanent audit suite or tracking backlog.

When a fix is implemented, integrate its regression beside the owning tests, demonstrate failure before/success after when feasible, and retire duplicate standalone checks. Do not encode an unresolved methodological choice as a permanent test contract.

Record actual runtime, OS, R/dependency versions, commands, failures and skips. Separate source inspection, personally executed synthetic checks, observed CI at a named revision, author-reported checks and remaining real-data validation. Investigate safe isolated alternatives if R/dependencies are unavailable. Give exact remaining maintainer commands and relevant vignette rebuilds with prerequisites and data-access implications; do not run real-data checks.

7. Reconcile issues and challenge findings

After independent discovery, review every open issue with its complete discussion, linked PRs and relevant sources. Record premise, current behavior, evidence, consequences, proposed solution’s adequacy, duplication, missing checks/decisions, recommended disposition and a substantive draft comment. Refresh the inventory before completion. A proposed fix is not a merged fix.

Have dialysis and transplant reviewers jointly challenge shared transitions and outcomes; claims and cost reviewers challenge aggregation and monetary measures; statistics and engineering reviewers challenge timing and representation; testing challenges all claimed guarantees. Correct unsupported findings and merge duplicates without losing distinct consequences.

For future capabilities, identify concrete research use, source feasibility, existing alternatives, why the capability belongs in the package, dependencies, priority and acceptance criteria. Distinguish enhancements from defects.

8. Deliver, preserve and integrate

Deliver a consolidated assessment with prioritized findings, issue-by-issue drafts, deduplicated new-issue proposals, scientific choices and alternatives, coverage/source records, reusable reproducers, concrete test/CI/documentation patches, validation limits and a staged roadmap.

Use REVIEWING.md’s Must fix / Should fix / Consider categories, separately from classification. Each finding needs a pinned location, evidence, consequence, confidence, proposed remedy and acceptance check. Serious findings need a reproducer or explicit verification blocker.

Keep full reports, reviewer transcripts, coverage ledgers and exploratory artifacts in permitted durable maintainer-accessible storage outside the repo. Temporary paths alone are insufficient. Preserve lasting knowledge in its existing home: reference background via reference/README.md, regression tests beside owning tests, user explanations in help/vignettes, process lessons in review guidance, and decisions in owning issues/implementation documentation. Do not create a second reference catalog, live backlog or repository audit archive.

Prepare concrete self-reviewed diffs for useful documentation improvements. Report each material result as integrated (link), proposed (patch/link), deferred (owning item and reason) or archive-only (reason). Keep analytical coverage, remaining validation and repository integration distinct. If coverage is incomplete, label the assessment partial; posting findings alone does not complete integration. End with what was preserved, where, and what remains.

9. Publication and follow-up permissions

Present the consolidated report before posting audit comments or new issues. Wait for explicit authorization for that posting step unless already supplied for the commissioned audit. Refresh revisions/discussions and deduplicate before posting; confirm writes succeeded. Use concise dated reassessments with pinned evidence, practical consequence and next step. Provide public synthetic reproducers where needed; never publish private conversations or archive links.

Preparing drafts, posting findings, installing tests, changing behavior and activating CI are distinct actions. Follow the maintainer’s permissions and per-file behavior-change approval rules. Do not close issues, formally approve or merge PRs, delete branches or change automation under this protocol. Automatic Claude review remains governed by its external configuration; this protocol does not enable it.
